_doc: Materials drop from monsters and feed crafting, skill/mod upgrades and trade. Gear bases are what recipes produce; the craft roll adds a Grade and options. Upgrade (+N) uses enhancement_stone and stays separate from Grade. Skill/mod ranks use skill_crystal. Per-base upgradeMaterial is retained only as the legacy salvage fallback for base crafting parts. shape = legacy shape hint; ground loot now uses authored art keyed by material ID; rare = light beam. Equipment itemLevel is persistent progression metadata, independent of grade, +N and stat wear requirements.

weaponTypes._doc: Every weapon type has a built-in (implicit) bonus. Some skills need a weapon type (skills.json requiresWeapon). hands: light = either hand (two light weapons dual-wield with no penalty), heavy = right hand only (a shield or nothing in the left), two = both hands (bow: arrows in the left). shield: true (the greatshield) is held in both hands and counts as the shield in hand: it blocks and Shield Bash works with it. Base stats follow handRules.baseFactor (two-hand 2.2x, a little more than two light weapons) x the light reference for the item level (base stats only, never options).

grades._doc: Grade adds unique affix slots: C 2, B 3, A 4, S 5. Base-stat variance is only -5% to +5%; enhancement is independent.

optionRoll._doc: Owner, 2026-10-25: a better grade rolls better options, and a higher item level rolls bigger ones. An option's range at item level L is its min..max times 1 + growth x (L - 1) (optionLevelGrowth: flat values grow like weapon base stats, percentages gently). Each grade rolls inside its band of that range (fractions of it); no grade passes the top. crafting.js optionRange.

optionLevelGrowth._doc: Per item level above 1. flat: 0.146 matches handRules.reference (perItemLevel / base), so a flat option keeps its share of a weapon's base stats (about 3.9x at item level 21). percent (a stat ending in Pct): about 1.5x at item level 21, so percentages stay modest. attribute (+STR ... +LUK): 0.05, so stat options reach about 2x at 21 and 4.5x at 70. fixed: no growth (life leech, which a small number already makes strong).

upgrade._doc: Guaranteed +1..+5, limited only by materials and gold. Each step adds 4% to base stats. Wearing a stronger item requires higher character stats, not a character level. Enhancement stones replace all monster-part/catalyst costs; grade promotion is unchanged.

gradeUpgrade._doc: Promote one grade retaining existing affixes and +N; add one unique affix, no level/stat gate to upgrading. Wearing uses the resulting actual item requirements.

requirements._doc: Wear requirements use every stat the character has (core/character.js statTotals), never the item's own bonus. A weapon, shield or armour piece (armor, helm, gloves, boots, on top of its level) asks for its requirementStat; one with a secondaryStat (its neighbour on the stat wheel, docs/STATS-TH.md) gives that stat secondaryShare of the requirement. Weighted actual item power above its C/+0 baseline plus a two-affix allowance increases the base requirement. All weights and growth are tunable here.

weaponIdentity._doc: Owner, 2026-10-29 (docs/STATS-TH.md; scripts/gear-identity.mjs, tests/core/stats.test.js): a weapon's stats follow the stats it asks for. A main-line weapon carries only damage (attack, or magic for staves, wands and INT weapons); a shield its guard stats. A main-and-secondary weapon deals its tier's damage (handRules reference) less damageCut and gains its secondary stat's identity (stats: AGI speed, DEX crit power, LUK crit chance, VIT HP, INT spell shield, STR attack) at base + perItemLevel x (item level - 1), times handScale of its hands, so percentages do not grow with weapon damage; a DEX/AGI dagger also gives up mainCut for DEX's identity. A main-and-secondary shield keeps its guard and adds the secondary identity. Greatshields already pair a VIT guard with STR attack.

armorIdentity._doc: Owner, 2026-10-29 (docs/STATS-TH.md; scripts/armor-identity.mjs, tests/core/stats.test.js): an armour piece's stats follow its class (the stat it asks for: VIT plate, AGI leather, INT cloth), measured against its slot's share of the balance model's set (progression.balance.gear defense and maxHp at its item level). core: multiples of that defense and HP (cloth turns the HP into a spell shield and MP). Plate is the toughest; leather trades some for speed and crit (a leather piece without either gains movement on body and feet, crit on head and hands); cloth carries a spell shield and MP. flavour: the piece's own percentages (speed, crit, healing ...) at that share of their cap (base + perItemLevel x (item level - 1), times capScale for small slots: gloves already carry attack or magic); other flavour stats (attack, magic, regeneration) stay as authored; the class's flavourCost of all flavour's power comes out of the core (leather least: speed is what it is for) (down to minCore of it). A crafted item level 1 piece is craftedStarter times a starter.

optionPools._doc: Owner, 2026-10-29 (docs/STATS-TH.md): a base rolls options from its class's pool (what that kind of item is for), plus its slot's extras for armour, so a robe never rolls bow damage. Classes: weapons by type (greatblades and axes are heavy; a mace is heavy, or priest when it asks for INT), shield for every offhand, armour by what it asks for (VIT plate, AGI leather, INT cloth), charm. Charms roll the widest pool, the only drop-find options and every stat. A starter item rolls its pool's first options at their minimum, so a pool starts with options that leave a starter wearable. scripts/option-pools.mjs writes each base's and recipe's optionPool from here; tests/core/stats.test.js checks they match.

handRules._doc: Weapon base power = baseFactor x reference(itemLevel). Reference is a light one-hand weapon: starter, or base + perItemLevel x (itemLevel - 1). Tested in tests/core/gear-hands.test.js. Dual wielding two light weapons needs the sum of both wear requirements.

offhandTypes._doc: Left-hand items that are not weapons.

arrows._doc: Arrows are spent by Attack+Projectile skills (perCast, plus multiShotExtra when a mod adds projectiles) and are crafted anywhere outside combat. With a bow, the arrows in use fill the left hand and add their stats. When the type in use runs out the next stocked type is used; with none, those skills cannot be cast.

consumables._doc: Potions bought at the town shop (town.shop) and used from the quick item slots. A potion restores flat + pct of the maximum, at once. Each group (hp, mp) has its own cooldown so one potion of each kind can be drunk back to back but not spammed. MP potions are an emergency aid (owner, 2026-10-27, docs/SKILL-GROWTH-TH.md phase 1): a long cooldown and a modest restore, so a build that spends MP hard pays for it with mana gear or Job Tree nodes, not with cheap potions (core/content-budget.js prices both). Stacks hold at most stackMax. New characters start with the start set; v7 saves receive it once.

shop._doc: The shopkeeper at town.shop sells these consumables for gold (price per item, items.consumables). Buy amounts are the quick choices offered in the shop panel.

salvage._doc: Town only. Salvage returns a grade share of the crafting recipe (rounded down, at least 1 of the main part). No base stone or crystal reward for any gear or grade, including starters. Sum current +N enhancement costs then return floor(total * upgradeReturn) per material; never refund gold. Legacy +N gear uses that same current-cost valuation because saves have no payment history. Existing inventory is never converted. Equipped and locked items are refused.

gearDrops._doc: Monsters drop gear made from their own parts (any recipe of the base uses one of the monster's drop materials), of the gear tier for the monster level (progression.balance.gearTiers; the nearest lower tier when none fits). A normal kill rolls each grade once, best first, at these chances; a boss always drops one item by weight. Starter gear never drops.
